articles.title: Jalen Hurts, A.J. Brown's Conversation Revealed in New NFL Rumors After Viral Video at Practice
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown shared an embrace at a joint practice after being urged to publicly reunite, according to Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown shared an embrace at a joint practice after being urged to publicly reunite, according to Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer.

McLane reported "both teams had wanted a made-for-the-cameras reconciliation and Brown... agreed when an intermediary intervened."

Chicken equity? This may be the wildest jersey number trade yet

94 WIP's Eliot Shorr-Parks shared a video Aug. 20 of Brown and Hurts sharing a hug and a conversation following a joint Eagles-Patriots practice.

According to McLane, the two "asked about each other's families, wished the other good luck in the coming season, and exchanged a few jokes, according to a source briefed on the interaction."

Hurts and Brown played six seasons and won Super Bowl LIX together before Brown was traded to the Patriots in June.

Brown said in a June interview with Maria Taylor he and Hurts were "not as close as we once were" but there was "still a lot of love" between them.

"I didn't truly understand why our friendship became the center of everybody's attention when it came to football because, looking back on it, we haven't been as close as we were a couple years now," Brown said.

Hurts, when asked in a recent interview with GQ's Zach Baron if he had grown apart from Brown, answered, "I mean, clearly."

The former Eagles teammates are not set to reunite this regular season. Brown is set to make his Patriots debut next Wednesday against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, while the Eagles are preparing to open the campaign the following Sunday against the visiting Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Shilo Sanders’ $11.89 million bankruptcy trial takes shocking turn as John Darjean collapses after hours of testimony
articles.summary: NFL News: John Darjean, the former school security guard seeking to keep an $11.89 million judgment against Shilo Sanders, collapsed in a Denver courtroom on Th.
articles.body: John Darjean, the former school security guard seeking to keep an $11.89 million judgment against Shilo Sanders, collapsed in a Denver courtroom on Thursday, September 3, after more than two hours of testimony. Darjean was taken to a hospital by ambulance and was released later that day, according to USA TODAY Sports. He did not return to court. The incident happened on Day 4 of Sanders’ bankruptcy trial, which is focused on whether the debt can be wiped out under Chapter 7 bankruptcy.Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial focuses on the 2015 school incidentThe case goes back to September 17, 2015, when Sanders was 15 and attending Focus Learning Academy in Dallas, Texas. Darjean was working as a school security guard and became involved after Sanders was removed from class for breaking school rules.Darjean has said Deion Sanders asked him to take Shilo’s phone. According to Darjean, Shilo became angry when he approached him and hit him with an elbow around the neck and chest area before punching him near the face. Darjean has said the incident caused serious damage to his neck and led to years of medical problems.Shilo Sanders has given a very different version. He has denied attacking Darjean and said he was trying to get away after Darjean grabbed and choked him. Sanders has said he blacked out during the struggle and had marks on his arms and neck afterward. He has continued to argue that he was defending himself.Police records from 2015 described the incident as an assault involving serious bodily injury, with Sanders listed as the suspect. Several school witnesses have also given accounts that support Darjean’s version. At the same time, Sanders’ side has presented testimony supporting his claim that Darjean was the aggressor.The dispute later moved to Texas state court. Darjean sued Sanders in 2016, and the case eventually went to trial in 2022. Sanders did not appear at that trial after dismissing his lawyers. A Dallas County judge then awarded Darjean $11,890,937.Shilo Sanders fights to erase the $11.89 million judgmentAfter Darjean began trying to collect the money, Shilo Sanders filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in Colorado in October 2023. The current case is not about deciding the original amount of the judgment. The bankruptcy court has already ruled that the Texas judgment establishes the cause of the injuries and the damages.Instead, Judge Michael E. Romero must decide whether Sanders’ actions were a “willful and malicious injury” under federal bankruptcy law. If the judge finds that they were, the $11.89 million debt cannot be discharged. If Sanders’ self-defense argument succeeds on the remaining issues, the debt could be wiped out through bankruptcy.The trial has included testimony from Darjean, Sanders and other witnesses, along with police and medical records from 2015. A witness for Sanders was also questioned about a recorded call in which her earlier account appeared to differ from her testimony in court.Deion Sanders had been expected to remain available for possible testimony, but Judge Romero released him from that requirement after deciding his testimony was not needed.The trial was scheduled to run through Friday, September 4. After the evidence is completed, Judge Romero will make the decision later in a written ruling.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aaron Donald's Status for Rams vs. 49ers Updated by Sean McVay Ahead of NFL Opener
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay is leaving Aaron Donald's status for Week 1 up in the air.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay is leaving Aaron Donald's status for Week 1 up in the air.

McVay told reporters that the upcoming week would be a "big week" for Donald as he assesses "how he feels."

"If he feels good enough to go, great," McVay said of the defensive tackle. "If not, I've got a lot of confidence in the other guys that'll be ready to step up if that's the case, that have really gotten all the reps anyways."

The Rams open the season against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday in Melbourne, so the clock is ticking to make a decision about Donald's status. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported earlier this week that the star playing in Week 1 might be a long shot, but added that it's "still on the table."

"I would say based on everything I've been told, a Week 2 or 3 debut looks more likely than Week 1," Graziano reported during a Tuesday appearance on NFL Live

McVay also emphasised last week that the team isn't rushing Donald back to the field and feels confident against the 49ers with or without him.

"What I think is really good for us is if he's able to go, great. If not, that's kind of how we've been operating as is," McVay told reporters . "And guys have done an excellent job of being able to do some really cool stuff in the meantime. And so, if he's not ready and that's not what's best for him and for the team, absolutely wouldn't have him playing Australia unnecessarily."

Even though Donald didn't join the Rams until late in training camp, he's managed to get back into football shape. ESPN's Sarah Barshop reported last week that after the Rams traded for Myles Garrett, Donald began putting himself through a "very strict, regimented process that was similar to what he did when he played," so he should be pretty warmed up at this point.

Donald also isn't expected to take on a strenuous workload, as Albert Breer of SI.com reported this week that he could play between 30 and 40 snaps per game.

Even if Donald isn't expected to take on the bulk of the defensive snaps, the Rams are surely being cautious with the 35-year-old. If he isn't 100 percent ready to go by Thursday, it sounds like he'll wait to make his season debut.

articles.title: Legendary sports agent talks about the Rams use of 'caponomics' to bring Aaron Donald out of retirement
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams used void years, backloaded contracts, and creative cap moves to fit Aaron Donald's $20 million deal alongside Myles Garrett and more.
articles.body: Aaron Donald officially made his return to the Los Angeles Rams earlier this week. But how did a team with so many expensive contracts fit Donald under the salary cap? According to famed sports agent Leigh Steinberg, it's because the Rams do a great job with "caponomics." The Rams did it by "creating cap room, redoing someone else's contract so that there's less salary involved and by giving that player a bonus," Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview. "If a team is creative, they can move other contracts around and create cap space." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE After falling short against their NFC West rival, the Seattle Seahawks, in the NFC Championship Game last season, the Rams went on a spending spree this offseason. They gave MVP-winning quarterback Matthew Stafford a one-year, $55 million contract extension, traded for Kansas City Chiefs star cornerback Trent McDuffie and signed him to a four-year, $124 million contract extension, signed cornerback Jaylen Watson to a three-year, $51 million contract, and acquired Cleveland Browns superstar Myles Garrett before signing him to a five-year, $208 million contract after redoing his deal following the trade. Despite handing out all of those massive deals, the Rams were still able to sign Donald to a one-year, $20 million deal, despite being up against the salary cap. So how, exactly, are the Rams making it work? Exactly as Steinberg said: by being creative. For Stafford’s deal, the Rams have pushed his contract further into the future, spreading out the cap hit using void years, meaning Stafford’s contract will count against the salary cap in even though he won’t be on the team. Stafford’s contract is spread out through the 2031 season. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! As for McDuffie, the Rams backloaded his contract. This season, McDuffie’s cap hit is just $10.8 million, but that rises to $30.8 million next season and will hover around that figure for ensuing three seasons. Garrett’s contract is structured similarly to both Stafford’s and McDuffie’s, with a lower cap hit in the first year and larger hits later in the deal while also using void years. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year’s contract runs through 2030, but his cap hits are spread through 2034. Here are his cap hits each year through 2034: $8.4 million, $15 million, $27.57 million, $39.875 million, $48.17 million, $17.523 million, $11.5 million, $7.6 million and finally $3.3 million. To fit Aaron Donald into their group of superstars, the Rams have pushed a lot of money into the future to make it work in the present. Steinberg thinks the decision to acquire Garrett and bring Donald out of retirement will be well worth it. "So let's imagine that you took a team that was already the favorite to win the Super Bowl because of their (trade) of the best defensive player in football, Myles Garrett. And you now add to him an unbelievably dominant defensive player in Aaron Donald," Steinberg said. PRO FOOTBALL HALL OF FAME MAKING MASSIVE OVERHAUL OF ITS SELECTION PROCESS FOLLOWING 2026 BILL BELICHICK SNUB "It creates an impregnable line that's impossible to double team. The synergistic effect of this is that an opposing offense can't double team both Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. So somewhere in there you're going to have this spectacularly dominant player on the loose." Steinberg is also certain that Donald, who made the Pro Bowl in each of his 10 seasons in the NFL, would not have returned unless he felt he could play at an elite level. "I am sure that Aaron Donald would not have come back except that he thought he could be dominant once again," Steinberg said. "I'm assuming that time takes its toll. Being outside of football takes its toll, but it won't take too long for Aaron Donald to be back in form. No other team has two players like this backed up by another three." In addition to having Donald and Garrett, the Rams’ defensive line was already strong with Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Byron Young and Poona Ford. Steinberg said the Rams’ defensive line could be one of the best of all time, comparing it to the legendary line the Baltimore Colts had in the 1960s. "I think the only thing that would be equivalent was the Fearsome Foursome that had Merlin Olsen and Deacon Jones and Rosie Greer. The Fearsome Foursome is back and as you said, they've got Poona Ford and Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske and Byron Young and they're loaded with gifted players," Steinberg said. CAM SKATTEBO CONSIDERED RETIREMENT AFTER SEASON-ENDING ANKLE INJURY IN GIANTS ROOKIE YEAR "The Rams do a better job of scouting players, drafting players, and then finding that one superstar that can be plugged into an already dominating defense or offense." A front comparable to the Fearsome Foursome of Olsen, Jones, Greer and Lamar Lundy would give the Rams an excellent chance of getting to the Super Bowl and winning it all. Steinberg, who was inducted into the California Sports Hall of Fame in 2017, has had many high-profile clients. Across football and baseball, Steinberg’s clients include Steve Bartkowski, Steve Young, Troy Aikman, Warren Moon, Bruce Smith, Thurman Thomas, Kordell Stewart, Jeff George, Ben Roethlisberger, Myron Rolle, Matt Leinart, Mark Brunell, Ricky Williams, Howie Long, Eric Karros and Dusty Baker, among others. Steinberg was not surprised that Donald came out of retirement because so many of his clients wanted to as well. "I had 64 first-round draft picks, 12 of the players in the Hall of Fame, and when they retired, they did it with class and dignity. But then a couple weeks later, the phone would ring and the player would say, ‘Do you think there's any spot for me? Do you think I can come back?’" Steinberg said. The legendary agent said these were players who had peaceful second careers lined up and had all the money they would need, but that they simply missed the game. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "They all want to play and when they're away from the game, players miss the structure, the fact that it gives them an itinerary that tells them what they're supposed to be doing every day, what they're supposed to be doing at this time of year. They have structure. They miss the camaraderie in the locker room with the band of brothers that are around them," Steinberg said. "They miss the electric excitement of performing in front of packed crowds and or many of them from Pop Warner on this is all they've known and so, like the moth to the flame, professional sports is so intoxicating that players never really want to retire." The Rams are certainly fortunate that Donald wanted to come back and play. The result could end with him holding another Lombardi Trophy.

articles.title: Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ Top Rookie Gets Promising Prediction for 2026

articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may have found a defensive difference-maker in Rueben Bain Jr., and one bold prediction has raised expectations for the rookie entering the 2026 season. The first-round pass rusher is being projected to challenge one of the NFL's longest-standing rookie sack records in his debut campaign.

Bain was selected 15th overall after establishing himself as one of college football's most productive defensive players at Miami. Despite concerns about his arm length and whether his physical measurements would translate against NFL competition, his production and ability to disrupt opposing offenses made him an attractive addition for a Buccaneers defense seeking more pressure off the edge.

The prediction calls for Bain to record 15 sacks as a rookie, which would surpass the NFL rookie record of 14.5 established by Jevon Kearse in 1999. Reaching that total would place the young defender in rare company and immediately establish him as one of the league's premier pass rushers.

Such a season would also provide a major boost to Tampa Bay's defensive outlook. The Buccaneers invested heavily in improving their front and now have an opportunity to pair experienced contributors with a young player capable of becoming a centerpiece of the pass rush for years to come.

articles.title: Bryce Young Gets Concerning Prediction Before 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Carolina Panthers are entering the 2026 season hoping Bryce Young can continue developing into the franchise quarterback they envisioned, but one bold pr...
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers are entering the 2026 season hoping Bryce Young can continue developing into the franchise quarterback they envisioned, but one bold prediction has raised the possibility of a dramatically different outcome. The projection suggests Young could lose his starting job during the season, creating a difficult question for a franchise that has invested heavily in his future.

Young has shown flashes of progress since arriving in Carolina, particularly as the offense has worked to provide him with better protection and more reliable playmakers. Still, entering his fourth NFL season means expectations have changed, and the Panthers will need to see sustained improvement from their former No. 1 overall pick.

The prediction calls for Carolina to bench Young before the end of the 2026 campaign. It also envisions the Panthers potentially turning elsewhere for help at quarterback, which would represent a major shift for an organization that has spent years trying to stabilize the most important position on the roster.

For Young , the season could become a defining test of whether his recent development can translate into consistent winning football. He must show greater command of the offense while limiting mistakes and producing enough explosive plays to keep pace in an increasingly competitive NFC.

Carolina Panthers' Bryce Young Predicted to Get Benched Ahead of 2026 NFL Season

Young received a worrying prediction ahead of the new NFL season . This is detailed more in an analysis by Douglas Clawson for CBS Sports.

Prediction: Bryce Young gets benched Bryce Young has slowly taken steps forward in the Panthers offense, capped by going worst to first in the abysmal NFC South last season. Perhaps the improvements have been exaggerated, though. He was 28th in the NFL in EPA per dropback last season and he will be benched in 2026 when he is unable to take Carolina to the next level. Patience will run thin, especially after the team made two big signings on defense in free agency (Devin Lloyd and Jaelan Phillips). The team picked up his fifth-year option this offseason, but the Panthers' brash owner David Tepper won't put up with a step backward from Young.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes injury recovery motivation was being able to walk before his daughter
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes set an unusual ACL surgery recovery goal after his knee injury: walking before his 11-month-old daughter Golden took her first steps.
articles.body: Professional athletes are simply built differently than normal people, and sometimes that manifests itself in a serious competitive nature. It's no secret that Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is a competitive guy, but I didn't realize just how much until a new report about his injury rehab over the offseason. It turns out the thing that drove him to get through his recovery after knee surgery was trying to walk before his 11-month-old daughter. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE An article by The Kansas City Star's Sam McDowell talks about how Mahomes' season came to an end last December when he injured his ACL and LCL in a game against the Los Angeles Chargers. The QB had surgery in Dallas, and after that the race was on to make sure he was back on his feet before his daughter was. "After he returned to Kansas City later in the week, he shared with some of those closest to him a more immediate goal for his recovery," McDowell wrote. "He wanted to walk before his baby daughter, 11-month-old Golden." Now, this is the reason (alright, one of many reasons) why Patrick Mahomes has won multiple Super Bowls, and you and I haven't. PATRICK MAHOMES LEAPS PAST DAK PRESCOTT AS NFL'S HIGHEST-PAID QB WITH RECORD CHIEFS EXTENSION WORTH $504.75M It's also why he has a golf course at his house, and I don't even have a putting mat... although I could order one on Amazon right now and it would be here at some point tomorrow. To be successful on a Mahomes-ian level, you have to be ultra-competitive, to the point where you're racing your kid in a made-up "who can walk first" contest. I bet there were moments where she stood up while holding onto the couch while he was still rocking an air cast, and he started sweating. At the end of the piece, it's revealed that Mahomes did get the job done and was up and walking before his kiddo took her first steps. Was there ever any doubt? articles.title: Sean McDermott Teases Possible NFL Return, Reveals 'Toughest Truth' from Bills Exit
articles.summary: Former Buffalo Bills head coach Sean McDermott confirmed that he's looking to return to the NFL sidelines.
articles.body:
Former Buffalo Bills head coach Sean McDermott confirmed that he's looking to return to the NFL sidelines.

"Look, I want to coach again," McDermott said during a Friday appearance on the Rich Eisen Show (3:50 mark). "I want to be a head coach in the NFL. I've got this burning desire in my heart to win a world championship and to take that to an organization and a fanbase. So, I owe that to myself but I also owe that to the next organization that I work for because I want to build on the success that we had in Buffalo."

He was also asked about his "toughest truth" following his departure from the Bills.

"I would say the hardest truth I got, and it hit me between the eyes, was sharing more of myself and sharing more of who Sean really is," McDermott said (4:40 mark). "And it's not that I didn't do that on a coaching level, but on a personal level. Like dropping my guard a little bit and just showing them my true self as a person."

The 52-year-old served as the Bills' head coach from 2017-25 before he was fired at the end of the 2025 season.

McDermott compiled a 98-50 record during his tenure in Buffalo, making eight playoff appearances.

The Bills struggled to emerge from the AFC despite their consistent postseason trips, as four of their past five playoff exits came in the divisional round.

articles.title: Former Cowboys Running Back Emmitt Smith is Sued by Investor Over Wind Farm Project
articles.summary: NFL career rushing leader Emmitt Smith is being sued by a Native American investment company over claims that the former Dallas Cowboys running back and his business partners misappropriated a $2.5 million loan that was supposed to fund a wind farm project in Texas.
articles.body:
NFL career rushing leader Emmitt Smith is being sued by a Native American investment company over claims that the former Dallas Cowboys running back and his business partners misappropriated a $2.5 million loan that was supposed to fund a wind farm project in Texas.

Kituwah LLC claimed in a lawsuit filed this week in Delaware that 4 13 Solutions used the money to repay an investor from previous dealings with Smith's company. Kituwah seeks to invest in business opportunities for the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians.

Kituwah's attorneys said Smith and the Pro Football Hall of Famer's longtime business partner, David Mosley, misrepresented their efforts to secure a U.S. Department of Energy loan that would have triggered repayment to Kituwah.

Bold Trade Predictions Before Season Kickoff 🏈

1 Reason Why Commanders' Fans Should Be Optimistic 🙏

Kituwah claims the loan has accrued about $600,000 in interest and is asking a jury to determine damages. A message sent to 4 13 Solutions wasn't immediately returned. There was no information on an attorney for Smith or his company in the filing.

According to the lawsuit, Darrel Wilson of Wilson Holdings of North America LLC told Kituwah that he accepted a $2.5 million payment from Smith's company and said he didn't know what triggered the payment. Kituwah's attorneys said it was, "Essentially, like a ponzi scheme."

Kituwah claims Wilson Holdings was supposed to be repaid only after the wind farm project between Austin and San Antonio, called Project Exodus, secured permanent financing.

"Smith and Mosley knew this was improper," the lawsuit said. "Instead of telling the truth, they represented to Kituwah that 4 13 Solutions had used the money to acquire Project Exodus as promised, but that the acquisition had been held up for one reason or another."

The lawsuit claims Smith and his partners never met the requirements for securing government funding and repeatedly made excuses for why the project wasn't proceeding or stopped responding to requests.

Kituwah said it delivered the funds on Sept. 1, 2023, with the expectation of being paid back within months. The lawsuit said 4 13 Solutions promised the wind farm would be operational by December 2024, but Kituwah had seen no evidence the project even existed just a month before that date.

Kituwah said Smith and his partners claimed the wind farm project was valued at $396 million and would generate nearly $14 million in net income in its first year.

The 57-year-old Smith spent the first 13 of his 15 seasons with the Cowboys, won three championships and was the MVP of Super Bowl 28. He broke Walter Payton's rushing record in 2002 and finished with 18,355 yards.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Reveals Giants Usage for 2026 NFL Season After Injury, Fantasy Impact and Draft Advice
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo is coming off a brutal injury during his rookie season, but the New York Giants running back is ready to take on a major workload this season.
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo is coming off a brutal injury during his rookie season, but the New York Giants running back is ready to take on a major workload this season.

Skattebo said that Giants head coach John Harbaugh asked if he's willing to take 20-plus carries a game, and he said he feels ready for it.

"I had a couple talks with him letting him know, hey, I'm gonna be ready to go. And he trusted me, and he trusted the fact that I'm ready to go," Skattebo said on Sports Seriously (3:00 mark). "He got a little snippet of it in our first preseason game, and he's gonna get a big snippet on Sunday Night Football. So I'm excited to show him what I have, and we talk a lot, but when he walks up to me and tells me, 'Are you ready for 20-plus carries a game?' I think I'm in a pretty good spot."

Skattebo's rookie season ended in Week 8 when he suffered a dislocated ankle, fractured fibula and a ruptured deltoid ligament against the Philadelphia Eagles. He had put together a solid season up to that point, recording 405 rushing yards, 207 receiving yards and seven total touchdowns.

His recovery from the injury wasn't easy, and he even said he considered retiring in the weeks after.

"Yeah, definitely," Skattebo said on Up & Adams . "I would say probably a month in, like the first month, I was like, 'Damn, do I really wanna do this?' And then, it was seven games. I was like, 'I gotta go back and play.' There's no shot. If it was the end of the year and I was like, 'Okay, I'm over this.' I didn't feel that way at all. ... I think that gave me an extra step of finding that deep place and coming out of a hole that I didn't know I could come out of."

Luckily for Giants fans, Skattebo stuck with his recovery and will be back for another year. Based on his recent comments, it sounds like he could be in for a big second season.

Skattebo will be competing with Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris and Devin Singletary for touches, but if Harbaugh asked him to take 20 touches per game, it seems he'll be a focal point of the offense.

That, of course, has fantasy implications. Skattebo likely won't be anyone's first running back selection, but if Harbaugh plans to use him often, he could be a reliable second option or a flex option.

Skattebo also excels through the air, making him a great choice for PPR leagues.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Praises Drake Maye's Arm Talent, Says Patriots QB Has 'Made My Job A Lot Easier'
articles.summary: The relationship between New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver A.J. Brown is off to a great start, as evidenced by their sitdown interview with Football Night in America analyst Devin McCourty, who asked how things are going so far (1:07 mark).
articles.body:
The relationship between New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver A.J. Brown is off to a great start, as evidenced by their sitdown interview with Football Night in America analyst Devin McCourty, who asked how things are going so far (1:07 mark).

Bold Trade Predictions Before Season Kickoff 🏈

1 Reason Why Commanders' Fans Should Be Optimistic 🙏

"He's made my job a lot easier. He's such a great guy. He always takes the blame for any little thing, and I'm like, 'Drake, it's OK, it's not that deep.'

"He's incredible, man. He's fun to play with, and I can't wait."

Brown added when asked how Maye makes his life easier: "His arm talent. He can make any throw from anywhere on the field."

"I think it's important with a player of AJ's caliber who's been in the league and has success in the league that he knows what it's like to be in the same page with the quarterback and knowing how important the relationships, not just on the field but off the field and knowing what he's seeing on film and not just going in separate position rooms and then talk about it, talk about it on the field, but talk about it outside of practice and outside of the game.

"And I think that's when it comes to life, those meetings, with him or with the receivers, me and the receivers, and those guys in there of what they're seeing, what I'm seeing, trying to get on the same page."

The Patriots were in the market for a No. 1 wide receiver after parting ways with Stefon Diggs, who led the team with 85 catches and 1,013 yards, last March. They found one in Brown, who arrived in town via trade on June 1 after the Pats sent a 2028 first-round draft pick and a 2027 fifth-round draft choice to the Philadelphia Eagles.

Brown has amassed 1,000 or more receiving yards in six of his seven seasons with the Tennessee Titans (2019-2021) and Eagles (2022-2025). He made the All-Pro Second Team each season from 2022-2024 as well. Last year, Brown ended with 78 catches for 1,003 yards and seven touchdowns.

It's clear Maye and Brown are getting along quite well so far, and we'll see how their partnership develops soon enough when the Pats face the host and Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday in a rematch of last season's Super Bowl, which the Seahawks won 29-13.

articles.body:
New England Patriots teammates A.J. Brown and Drake Maye reacted to a viral photo of Brown wearing a jersey of franchise icon Tom Brady as a child.

"Look at that," Maye said with a laugh in their interview with NBC Sports' Devin McCourty (8:35 mark).

"He'd have that number one, probably," Maye said (8:51 mark).

Brown and Maye are entering their first season on the same roster after New England acquired the star wide receiver in a June 1 trade with the Philadelphia Eagles.

While Brown is a Mississippi native, he's explained that Brady is his favorite player in NFL history and cried when the Patriots selected N'Keal Harry over him in the 2019 draft (h/t Zack Cox of the Boston Herald ).

Brown will now attempt to help New England remain a contender in the AFC after making a Super Bowl appearance last season. Maye was a key reason for the Patriots' success, finishing No. 2 in MVP voting .

In 17 starts, he completed 72.0 percent of his throws for 4,394 yards and 31 touchdowns compared to eight interceptions. Maye also rushed for 450 yards and four scores.

The Patriots will open their 2026 campaign with a Super Bowl rematch against the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday. Kickoff is at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Chiefs C Creed Humphrey Has Favorable Odds to Win NFL Honor
articles.summary: If there’s one thing you can count on happening for the Kansas City Chiefs this season, it’s center Creed Humphrey being great.A second-round draft pick in 2...
articles.body:
If there's one thing you can count on happening for the Kansas City Chiefs this season, it's center Creed Humphrey being great.

A second-round draft pick in 2021, Humphrey was great right off the jump. He has been the heart and soul of the Chiefs' offensive line, helping them win back-to-back Super Bowls. Humphrey is a three-time All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowler.

Kansas City Chiefs C Creed Humphrey May Have Most Valuable Odds to Win NFL Protector of the Year in 2026

Iain MacMillan of Sports Illustrated recently examined the odds from FanDuel for NFL Protector of the Year in 2026. The sportsbook currently has Humphrey at +1500, the sixth-highest odds among all offensive linemen. MacMillan believes given those odds and Humphrey's skills, that is a great bet to make.

"That leads me to Creed Humphrey, the center for the Kansas City Chiefs. He has long been looked at as one of the best centers in the NFL, and he was named a finalist for the award last season. If the Chiefs bounce back in 2026 and return to the playoffs, and if Humphrey's play at center ends up being a pivotal factor in that, I could see the voters giving him the nod."

Barring injury, it's hard to imagine Humphrey not being a finalist for the award again this year. If the Chiefs revitalize their rushing attack with Kenneth Walker III pounding the rock, that will help Humphrey's chances all the more. Winning Protector of the Year would pretty much complete Humphrey's already Hall of Fame-worthy resume.

Chiefs' Interior OL Could Be Best in the NFL

While Kansas City has some question marks at the offensive tackle spots , the interior (guards and centers) looks stellar. We know how great Humphrey is, and next to him is two-time Pro Bowl right guard Trey Smith . Humphrey and Smith entered the NFL together, and were given big-time contract extensions by the Chiefs.

Over at left guard is third-year man Kingsley Suamataia. After not fitting in as an offensive tackle during his rookie season, he found his niche at guard. Suamataia improved steadily throughout 2025, and could be poised to join Humphrey and Smith as a Pro Bowler this season. The Chiefs also have nice depth behind those three in center Hunter Nourzad, as well as guards Mike Caliendo and Joshua Ezeudu.

articles.title: ‘This isn’t good’: Buffalo Bills turf raises concerns before season opener
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are playing in a brand-new stadium this year. While that should be a reason for excitement and something both the team and its fans can loo...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are playing in a brand-new stadium this year. While that should be a reason for excitement and something both the team and its fans can look forward to ahead of opening day, the new venue has already come with its fair share of issues.

Over the last several weeks, the Bills have faced criticism over hundreds, and potentially thousands, of seats that feature obstructed views. Now, the team has another issue to deal with: the playing surface.

After enduring negative headlines and criticism from fans over the seats with obstructed views , the Bills are now dealing with another embarrassing issue as the grass field at their brand-new $2.2 billion stadium has begun falling apart.

Following only two preseason games, the Bills removed the entire grass field that had been installed in October 2025. The grass roots, however, apparently failed to properly take hold, with large sections of sod repeatedly being torn up by players during the two preseason contests and two open practices at the stadium.

In an article published by The Athletic this week, several experts expressed concerns about the condition of the field.

"I saw their press release and heard some of their rationale, and they probably ought to start their stories 'Once upon a time,'" said an award-winning sports agronomist who has helped install dozens of NFL and college football fields over the decades. "That's the worst sod I've seen in the NFL in my career. I can't even imagine how that could have happened."

Although natural grass is generally considered a safer option than artificial turf, one expert does not believe that was true in this particular situation, considering the poor condition of the field.

"Yes, natural turf is safer in a perfect setting," said Tony Dick, a sports management professor at Baldwin Wallace University and former Cleveland Browns assistant head groundskeeper. "But if you have the situation like you have in Buffalo — and I went back and watched the film — you cannot tell me that field was safer than the artificial turf they just left.

"I'm never putting Josh Allen on a field in that condition," he continued.

With the grass already coming apart just weeks ahead of the NFL season, the Bills are now working against the clock to get new sod installed. The team's season-opening matchup with the Detroit Lions on "Thursday Night Football" is only two weeks away, and that game will begin a stretch of three consecutive contests at the new Highmark Stadium over just 18 days.

The experts who spoke with The Athletic expect the replacement turf to be ready and capable of holding up for the season opener against the Lions, but what happens beyond that is much less certain.

"They will have a difficult time," the anonymous agronomist said. "There's so much going wrong, and there's so little time. If that field makes it through the second game, I'll be shocked."

Dick, meanwhile, believes the Bills could ultimately be forced to abandon the natural grass field altogether.

"You might have artificial turf back in there within three years," Dick said. "Just because it's safer than whatever that was."

Needless to say, the concern from experts has led to concerns from the sports world.

"OK, I said it looks cool as hell but you can't have *this*, either. I'll never accept that there's just no solution. I can see all the soccer pitches in Europe from my back yard," wrote soccer commentator Ryan Burns .

"I'm sticking to my completely fabricated theory that the stadium is cursed. Mainly because I have way too much free time," wrote sportswriter Rhys Scott .

"Owners hesitant to switch to natural grass likely are monitoring this closely. Players have lobbied for natural grass, but this isn't good," wrote Mike Jones of The Athletic.

"I get the feeling Bills fans should enjoy seeing games on grass while they can. Seems like the possibility of going back to artificial turf is very real in the next couple years. Makes no sense, if Green Bay can manage, Buffalo should too," wrote football commentator Helmet Addict .

"Cursed franchise," wrote prominent Kansas City Chiefs content creator Clay Wendler .

It will certainly be interesting to see how the turf holds up this season.
